messages.content: What workload, freshness, permission and latency constraints are you designing for, and what do they imply?
The service needs fresh, permission-aware answers with source citations, predictable latency and controlled cost. I would plan ingestion and query capacity separately.
How do documents become searchable and how will edits and deletes propagate?
Incremental connectors feed structure-aware chunking and versioned embeddings into keyword and vector indexes. Hybrid retrieval combines lexical and semantic signals.
How do retrieval results turn into a grounded answer, and what happens with weak evidence?
ACL-filtered hybrid retrieval feeds a cross-encoder reranker and context builder. Grounded generation produces source-linked answers with citation validation and abstention.
What happens when the vector index or model service fails, and how do replicas recover?
Replicas, circuit breakers, backpressure and replay protect the ingestion and retrieval pipeline. The generation path has timeout handling and bounded retries.
How will you measure cost per question and trace a bad answer?
Model routing, semantic caching and prompt caching control cost. Distributed tracing records retrieval, reranking and generation, with cost per question on the dashboard.
Which retrieval and answer metrics will you evaluate before shipping a change?
I measure faithfulness via LLM-as-judge on a golden set, retrieval Recall@k and citation precision. Human review checks the judge and regression evaluations gate releases.
How does a revocation take effect within five minutes, how are cache keys scoped, and how do you handle malicious retrieved instructions?
Permission-aware caching, ACL invalidation and retrieval filters protect access. Guardrails, prompt isolation and audit logs protect the generation path.
What workload, token and GPU capacity do you need at Senior?
I would plan capacity in input and output tokens, distinguish prefill from decode and account for peak demand. The scheduler controls GPU admission.
How will you store conversation history and keep context bounded?
A user-partitioned conversation store backs a context builder with truncation, summarization and prompt caching. User deletion propagates to conversation records and summaries.
How do batching, KV cache and stream recovery work in your design?
Continuous batching and KV-cache management support inference. SSE streams answers with persisted progress, reconnect handling and idempotency keys.
What happens when GPUs are full or a node dies midway through an answer?
Bounded queues, tier-aware admission and graceful degradation protect the GPU fleet. Replicas and retries support interrupted generations.
How will tier routing, cost per message and model rollout work?
The inference router selects large and small models by tier and task. Token accounting tracks cost per message, while canary deployment and rollback protect releases.
Which quality and safety metrics determine whether a new model can ship?
I measure faithfulness via LLM-as-judge on a golden set, helpfulness through human ratings and quality through regression evaluations. Release gates use those signals.
How do input/output moderation and ownership checks work without violating first-token latency?
Input moderation, streamed-output guardrails and conversation ownership checks enforce safety. The pipeline records safety decisions and protects user isolation.
What scope, task limits and mistake constraints matter for this agent?
I would separate read and write tools, treat incorrect writes as serious incidents and apply task budgets. The orchestrator controls delegated execution.
How does the agent loop choose and validate tools, and when does it stop?
A planner and durable agent runner use a schema-validated tool registry. Tool selection, loop detection and step limits control the execution loop.
How do checkpoints and idempotency avoid duplicate emails after an ambiguous timeout?
Idempotency keys, durable checkpoints and an action ledger support safe retries. The runner restores persisted task state and reconciles tool outcomes.
How would you investigate a wrong action from yesterday?
An audit log, correlated traces and replay capture the agent run. Tool contracts, decisions and execution outcomes support incident investigation.
What latency budget and cost per task do you expect?
Token budgets, model routing and tool latency tracing control task economics. Dashboards show cost per task and end-to-end completion latency.
What mocked-tool scenarios and metrics gate a new model or prompt?
I measure task success, wrong-action rate and faithfulness via LLM-as-judge on a golden set. Mocked tools, human review and regression gates validate model and prompt releases.
What exactly does the approval show, whose credentials execute the action, and what if retrieved content tries to authorize a write?
Delegated scoped credentials, exact-action approval and recipient policies protect writes. Prompt isolation, guardrails and audit trails separate retrieved content from execution authority.
